;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**[[Nguetchewe attack]]
***Suspected [[Boko Haram]] militants attack an [[IDP camp]] with a [[grenade]] in [[Far North Region, Cameroon|Far North]], [[Cameroon]], killing 16 people and wounding six others. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-nigeria-security-boko-haram-cameroon/suspected-boko-haram-militants-kill-15-in-northern-cameroon-idUSKBN24Y0B3?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Business and economy
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**The [[government of Syria|Syrian government]] condemns a deal signed between Delta Crescent Energy, a U.S. oil firm and [[Kurds in Syria|Kurdish]] rebels of the [[Syrian Democratic Forces]] (SDF) to manage the [[Kurds|Kurdish]]-controlled northeastern oil fields. The statement says the deal is "stealing" Syrian [[crude oil|crude]]. On Thursday, [[U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Mike Pompeo]] said the U.S. is supportive of the deal. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-syria-oil-usa/syria-says-u-s-oil-firm-signed-deal-with-kurdish-led-rebels-idUSKBN24Y0FD?il=0 (Reuters)] [https://oilprice.com/Latest-Energy-News/World-News/Syrian-Kurds-Ink-Oil-Deal-with-US-Company.html (Oil Price)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[Hurricane Isaias]]  
***A [[Saffir–Simpson scale|tropical storm]] with maximum sustained winds of 65 mph (100 km/h), Isaias is less than a mile off the [[Cape Canaveral Air Force Station]] on Florida's [[Atlantic Ocean|Atlantic Coast]], moving north-northwest at about 8 mph (13 km/h). Tropical storm warnings have been issued as far north as [[Surf City, North Carolina]]. [https://www.orlandosentinel.com/weather/hurricane/os-ne-tropical-storm-isaias-sunday-update-20200802-pygkkz75dvdidngvdzgkrf7wxq-story.html (''Orlando Sentinel'')] [https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/text/refresh/MIATCPAT4+shtml/021450.shtml (National Hurricane Center)]
***Earlier this week, one man was killed in the [[Dominican Republic]], when a power line fell on his horse, killing both the rider and the animal, and a woman was killed in [[Puerto Rico|Puerto Rican]] flooding while crossing a bridge. The storm has resulted in uprooted trees, destroyed crops and homes, and widespread flooding and small landslides. [https://weather.com/safety/hurricane/news/2020-07-30-tropical-storm-isaias-puerto-rico-dominican-republic-haiti-impacts (The Weather Channel)]
*[[Apple Fire]]
**Nearly 8,000 people are evacuated from the town of [[Cherry Valley, California]], [[United States]], due to a growing [[wildfire]]. The Apple Fire has burned over 20,500 acres and is five percent contained. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2020/08/03/apple-fire-cherry-valley-grows-near-beaumont-evacuations-ordered/5571071002/ (''USA Today'')]
*The [[United States Marine Corps]], [[United States Navy|Navy]], and [[United States Coast Guard|Coast Guard]] halt a massive search and rescue operation for seven Marines and Navy sailors who went missing on Thursday off the coast of [[San Clemente Island]] in California. All the missing are now presumed dead. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/health/2020/08/02/missing-marines-sailor-presumed-dead-search-halted/5566410002/ (''USA Today'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[Government of India|India]]'s [[Minister of Home Affairs (India)|Minister of Home Affairs]], [[Amit Shah]], tests positive for COVID-19 and is admitted to hospital. [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/coronavirus/2020/08/02/Coronavirus-India-s-Interior-Minister-tests-positive-for-COVID-19.html (Al Arabiya)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****[[President of the Philippines|President]] [[Rodrigo Duterte]] reimposes [[COVID-19 community quarantines in the Philippines|modified enhanced community quarantine]] (MECQ), one of the strictest lockdown measures on [[Metro Manila]] and the surrounding provinces of the Philippine capital for 15 days. [https://rappler.com/nation/coronavirus-cases-philippines-august-2-2020 (Rappler)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Hawaii]]
****A [[Thai Armed Forces|military]] spokesman says that plans to undertake joint military exercises with the U.S. military have been suspended after nine Thai soldiers who returned from [[Hawaii]] tested positive for COVID-19. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavius-thailand/thai-army-suspends-u-s-training-plans-after-soldiers-contract-covid-19-idUSKBN24Y0E9?il=0 (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]], [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns]]
***[[Premier of Victoria|Victorian premier]] [[Daniel Andrews]] declares a state of disaster across the state and imposed stage 4 lockdown in Metropolitan [[Melbourne]]. The new measures include nighttime [[curfew]], which will be implemented across Melbourne from 20:00 to 05:00 ([[Time in Australia|AEST]]). The restrictions comes into effect at 18:00 (6 p.m.) and last until September 13. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-australia-53627038 (BBC News)]
***The rest of [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] places under stage three restrictions and will take effect on August 6. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-08-02/victoria-coronavirus-restrictions-imposed-death-toll-cases-rise/12515914 (ABC News Australia)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic on cruise ships]]
***At least 40 passengers and crew from the [[MS Roald Amundsen|MS ''Roald Amundsen'']] cruise ship test positive for COVID-19 after two recent Arctic voyages. Health authorities are trying to trace other passengers that may be infected. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-norway-cruiseship/at-least-40-infected-with-covid-19-on-norway-cruises-amid-scramble-to-trace-passengers-idUSKBN24Y0LO?il=0 (Reuters)]

***Hundreds of people gather and protest in [[Portland, Oregon]], marking the 66th night of protests in the city. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/02/us/portland-protests/index.html (CNN)]
